local_derivations: At most k-1 primes at or above rho^k can be forbidden by earlier greedy base terms: such a divisor must equal its selected term.
The corrected prime count in [rho^k,rho^(k+1)] exceeds k and gives a_k=O_rho(rho^k).
The interval [rho^k,rho^k(1+k^-2)] contains more than k primes eventually; summable relative errors give rho^s<=h_s<=C_rho rho^s.
The prime-base limiting construction has O(N(log N)^4/(log log N)^2) time, independently of the fixed-rho bound.
